It is my pleasure to write this letter on behalf of Jordan Doe, who is
applying for a position in your department. Jordan is a Ph.D. candidate
in the Social Science program at Caltech and is on track to complete
the doctorate by the end of this academic year. I have known Jordan
since they entered the program and have taught them in several courses.
I am confident that Jordan is one of the strongest candidates on the
market this year, and I recommend them to you in the strongest possible
terms.

Jordan's research lies at the intersection of law, economics, and
political science. The work combines sophisticated causal inference and
applied statistics with important substantive questions about housing
law, eviction, and the operation of courts. The job market paper
exemplifies this integration: the data are newly assembled, the causal
identification strategy is clean, and the discussion of mechanisms is
nuanced and compelling.

The broader dissertation expands this research agenda in several
important directions, using a regression discontinuity design to test
whether court-drawn district boundaries create local inequities in
access to justice. In a related methodological paper, Jordan develops
robust approaches to RD estimation when the standard smoothness
assumptions may not hold.

Beyond the technical contributions, Jordan is an exceptional teacher and
a generous colleague. They have served as a teaching assistant for our
graduate sequence in quantitative methods, where students consistently
rate them among the best instructors they have had. Jordan also
organizes our applied statistics reading group and has mentored several
junior students through their first research projects.

In short, Jordan combines technical depth, substantive importance, and
genuine collegiality in a way that is rare among candidates at this
stage. I expect Jordan to become a leader in the field, and I recommend
them without reservation. Please do not hesitate to contact me if I can
provide any further information.
